2  -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:24945  MFA No. 2873 of 2015  C/W RP No. 170 of 2018  THIS RP IS FILED UNDER ORDER 47 RULE 1 OF CPC,
PRAYING TO REVIEW THE ORDER DATED:21/03/2018 PASSED IN MFA No. 3220/2015 (MV), ON THE FILE OF THE HON'BLE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA, BENGALURU.

THIS APPEAL AND PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA No.2873/2015 is filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.594/2012 dated 28.08.2014 by the Court of I Addl. District Judge & II MACT, Tumkur, seeking for reduction of the quantum of compensation.
2. Review Petition No.170/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company seeking review of the order passed in MFA No.3220/2015 dated 21.03.2018 passed by this Court on the ground that there is an error apparent on the face of the record that the percentage of disability taken as 100% by this Court, is on higher side.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that the claimant had sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 23.02.2012 at about 8.00 p.m., near NC: 2023:KHC:24945 Bettadahalli on Chelur-Hosakere Road when a Hero Honda Splendor Plus motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-06/V-9994 dashed against the bicycle of the claimant.
Therefore, the claimant has preferred claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act, seeking compensation.

4. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
5.
MFA No.2873/2015 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal for reducing quantum of compensation
, likewise, the claimant has also filed MFA No.3220/2015 before this Court for seeking enhancement of compensation.

This Court by order dated 21.03.2018, has disposed of the MFA No.3220/2015 and reducing the quantum of compensation from Rs.8,71,000/- to Rs.5,22,600/- on the ground that the contributory negligence held at 50% by the Tribunal is little bit on higher side and reduced to 40% but the percentage of disability is taken as 100% and accordingly, awarded NC: 2023:KHC:24945 compensation of Rs.7,56,000/- under the head 'loss of future income due to disability and among this amount, 40%
deducted then it amounts to Rs.4,53,600/- and accordingly, awarded.
6.

Further, the Insurance Company as per review petition stated that there is an error apparent on the face of record that the doctor has given evidence that claimant had suffered 70% of disability towards right lower limb and 24% disability towards whole body, but this Court

sentences.text: the appeal filed by the claimant has taken 100% disability.
Therefore, awarded compensation of Rs.4,53,600/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
7. The appeal and review petition are filed by the Insurance Company pertaining to the same accident, claimant and respondents.
Therefore, they are taken together for common consideration.
An error is apparent on the face of record regarding consideration of percentage of disability to the whole body in the appeal NC: 2023:KHC:24945 filed by the claimant in MFA No.3220/2015.
Even though this Court has held the contributory negligence of 40% on the part of the claimant, but has committed an error in considering 100% disability suffered by the claimant.
The PW-2, who is treated doctor, has stated that the claimant had suffered 70% of the physical disability towards right lower limb and 24% towards whole body.
The claimant had suffered fracture of right femur.

Therefore, certainly this fracture do not cause 100% disability to the claimant and the assessment of disability at 70% to the right lower limb and 24% towards whole body as deposed by the doctor is correct.
Therefore, by applying the principle of law laid down in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, the functional disability is taken as 25% to the whole body.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the quantum of compensation determined by this Court in MFA No.3220/2015 is liable to be reviewed/modified.
NC: 2023:KHC:24945 8.

Since the claimant had suffered functional disability of 25% to the whole body as discussed above and as per decision of this Court in New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar in MFA No.103807/2016 c/w MFA Nos.103835/2016 and 103807/2018 dated 27.05.2022, certain quantum of income has to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life'
since disability suffered by the claimant significantly at the age of 42 years affects his earning capacity.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar in MFA No.103807/2016 c/w MFA Nos.103835/2016 and 103807/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, 25% of income is to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life' due to injury and disability sustained.
The notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.4,500/- per month.
The claimant was aged about 42 years.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is '14'.

Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is re-assessed and quantified as Rs.2,36,250/-
(4,500 + 1,125 (25% of 4,500) x 25% x 14 x 12).
NC: 2023:KHC:24945 9.
This Court has awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards 'Pain and sufferings' which is just and proper.
Hence, the same is kept intact.
10. The compensation of Rs.25,000/- awarded under the head 'Medical Expenses' is as per the medical bills produced by the claimant and the same is kept intact.
11. This Court has not awarded any compensation under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period', which is an error apparent on the face of record.
The claimant was working as a Coolie and due the fracture of right femur, he might have not attended to his work for atleast six months.
It is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.27,000/- (4,500 x 3 months) under the said head.

The Manager vs Lokesh on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25983353/
4 12.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head 'Loss of Amenities'.
It is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the said head.
This Court has awarded a lesser sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'Food and nourishment'.

The same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
14.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:
 SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 60,000  (intact)
 2.

Medical expenses 25,000  (intact)
 3. Loss of future income due to 2,36,250  disability  4. Food and nourishment 20,000  5. Loss of Amenities 50,000  6. Loss of income during laid up 27,000  period

15 . This Court in MFA No.3220/2015 has awarded the compensation of Rs.,8,71,000/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,18,250/- along with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization.

Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, which is under challenge in the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is modified and also at the same time, the order passed by this Court in MFA No.3220/2015 is reviewed by modifying some errors apparent on record.

17. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
MFA No.2873/2015 and R.P.No.170/2018 are allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.594/2012 dated 28.08.2014 by the Court of I Addl. District Judge & II MACT, Tumkur is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,18,250/-
along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
